region.settingsSubtitle: The language of the app and the coach, your country for price references, and the time zone for your reminders.

landing.tagline: To eat better every day, without the hassle. It gives you a flexible guide in the morning, reviews the day with you at night, and turns your goal into progress you can see.
landing.bullet1: Habits and wellbeing, never rigid diets
landing.bullet2: A measurable goal with visual progress and streaks
landing.bullet3: Relaxed, neutral or demanding tone: you choose
landing.disclaimer: A flexible wellbeing guide. Calories and macros are rough estimates, not exact nutritional tracking. It does not replace medical advice.

intro.title:
Eat well
without the mental load
intro.body: Every morning you know what you'll eat. Every night you review it in a minute. Your plan and your family's adapt. Nothing else.
intro.disclaimer: A wellbeing guide, not a diet. Calorie figures are rough estimates.

name.text: Hi, I'm Peppers, your AI food assistant. I'll be with you every day with flexible ideas, never rigid diets or pressure. To start, what should I call you?

birthdate.text: What's your date of birth? That way your age updates on its own and I adapt the menu as the years go by.
birthdate.hint: Pick the day on the calendar

bio.text: Nice to meet you. Tell me your biological sex, current weight and height.

pregnancy.text: Are you pregnant or breastfeeding right now?
pregnancy.hint: It changes what's safe to recommend

cycle.text: Do you notice your menstrual cycle affecting your appetite, energy or cravings?
cycle.hint: E.g.: I snack more in the days before my period (or 'I don't notice it' / 'I'd rather not say')

medical.text: Any medical condition, medication or supplement I should keep in mind?
medical.hint: Optional: conditions under medical supervision, medication that affects appetite or energy, and supplements (protein, creatine, vitamins...). If there's nothing, tap Skip

allergies.text: Do you have any food allergies or intolerances?
allergies.hint: If there are none, just say 'none'

allergySeverity.text: Of those allergies or intolerances, is any of them severe (anaphylaxis-type), or are they milder?
allergySeverity.hint: E.g.: shellfish is severe, lactose I can manage

activity.text: How would you describe your usual physical activity, and what exercise do you do?
activity.hint: Baseline level (sedentary, active, very active...) plus type and frequency. E.g.: desk job, but I go to the gym 3 days a week and play padel on Sundays

schedule.text: What's your work or daily schedule like? Fixed shifts, travel, office...
schedule.hint: E.g.: office from 9 to 6, I travel one week a month

mealsPerDay.text: How many meals do you usually have a day at the moment?

mealsToPlan.text: Which meals do you want me to plan and include in your shopping?

cooking.text: Do you usually cook, or do you often eat out or order in? Tell me which days and meals.
cooking.hint: E.g.: I cook dinner Monday to Friday and eat out at lunchtime

kitchen.text: What do you have in your kitchen?

cookingSkill.text: How do you get on with cooking?

dietPattern.text: Do you follow any eating pattern?

foods.text: Is there any food you're not willing to give up, and any you don't want to see on your plate?
foods.hint: What's non-negotiable (e.g.: my morning latte) and what you won't eat (e.g.: coriander, liver, oily fish). If there's nothing for either, say so.

cuisine.text: What kind of food do you like most?

foodRelationship.text: How would you describe your relationship with food these days?
foodRelationship.hint: No filters, nothing gets judged here

chips.noTime: No time to think about it

edHistory.text: Before we go on: do you have now, or have you had in the past, a very difficult relationship with food — bingeing, very strict restriction, purging? I'm asking so I can support you better, never to judge you.
edHistory.hint: No filters, nothing gets judged here

livesWith.text: Who do you live with? Tell me if you share meals with anyone and which ones (for example, you always have dinner together).
livesWith.hint: E.g.: I live with my partner, we have dinner together every day

partnerApp.text: Will your partner use Peppers too? If they install it, you can join up in Your home and share meals and shopping.
partnerApp.hint: That tells me whether the budget you give me later is just yours or for both of you

kids.text: Are there children at home? Tell me their ages, allergies or intolerances and how they eat.
kids.hint: Optional: if there are no little ones, tap Skip

othersDiet.text: Does anyone else at home have allergies, intolerances or something they don't eat?

portions.text: How many portions do you normally cook for each meal?
portions.hint: E.g.: 2 on weekdays, 4 on Saturday — it can vary

targetWeight.text: What weight would you like to settle at? If you're already there, give me that number.

trainingExperience.text: Since your goal is to build muscle: how much strength training experience do you have?

numbers.text: Do you want to see calories and macros in the app?
numbers.hint: Dishes are calculated the same either way. You can change this any time in Settings.

chips.hide: No, I'd rather not see them

deadline.text: When would you like to reach that weight? No pressure — it's to work out a healthy pace.
deadline.hint: E.g.: by June, in 6 months, no rush

scope.text: Apart from weight, do you want my help with anything else?

struggles.text: What have you found hardest to keep up in previous attempts? And while we're at it: have you tried counting calories or macros before, or other diets? Did it help, or did it become an obsession?
struggles.hint: Knowing this helps me avoid repeating what doesn't work for you

budget.text: How much time do you have to cook each day, and how much do you want to spend on food a month?
budget.hint: E.g.: 20 min a day and about 250 {{currency}} a month

budgetHousehold.text: How much time do you have to cook each day, and what's the household's TOTAL monthly food budget (including your partner)?
budgetHousehold.hint: Since your partner won't use the app, we'll plan the shopping for both of you. E.g.: 20 min a day and about 400 {{currency}} a month in total

tone.text: Would you rather I was more encouraging and relaxed, or more demanding and direct?

times.text: Last one: what time would you like your morning summary and your evening review?

intro.title: Let's get to know you
intro.body: It's about {{count}} questions (~10 minutes). You can skip any of them, go back and change whatever you like — and if you stop halfway, you pick up right where you left off.

nightly.title: Today's review
nightly.subtitle: Less than a minute, no marks and no exam.
nightly.pendingBody: {{meals}} — if you're done for today, you can simply close them; they don't count as a failure.

full.relajado: A perfect day, without even trying. Enjoy it.
full.exigente: A complete day — that's how a good month is built.

partial.relajado: Part of the day went well, and that already counts. No more sums.
partial.neutro: A partial day. What you did counts too.
partial.exigente: Half a day — tomorrow you can finish it properly.

none.relajado: Today wasn't the day, and that's fine. Tomorrow is another day.
none.neutro: Nothing was logged today, no drama.
none.exigente: Today stayed at zero — tomorrow it's time to pick it back up.

up.relajado: This week is going better than the last ({{thisWeek}}% vs {{lastWeek}}%) — notice what worked.
up.neutro: Weekly trend: {{thisWeek}}%, against {{lastWeek}}% last week. You're improving.
up.exigente: A week on the rise: {{thisWeek}}% vs {{lastWeek}}%. Keep pushing.

down.relajado: This week has been a bit harder ({{thisWeek}}% vs {{lastWeek}}%), and that's okay. Not every week is the same.
down.neutro: This week: {{thisWeek}}%, a little below last week's {{lastWeek}}%.
down.exigente: This week drops to {{thisWeek}}% (it was {{lastWeek}}%). Time to readjust, not to give up.

flat.relajado: This week is much like the last ({{thisWeek}}%). Calm consistency.
flat.neutro: This week: {{thisWeek}}%, similar to last week.
flat.exigente: A steady week at {{thisWeek}}%. To go up, one more push each day.

closing: Tomorrow is a blank page. Today you've done what you could.
You don't need a perfect day, just a day you tried.
Every meal you log is information to do better, not an exam.
Rest. The body moves forward while it sleeps too.
What counts isn't today alone, it's the whole week.
One more step, even if today's was small.
